title: After a fall — the next few days
text: Bruising and stiffness are normal for a few days and can limit movement. Rest, but keep moving gently around the house. Drink fluids regularly. Note any new pain, swelling or difficulty walking and tell the GP. Keep a phone within reach at all times.
source: WA Health, Health advice following a fall

title: Possible head knock — what to watch for (24 to 72 hours)
text: Someone should stay with the person, or check on them regularly, for the next 24 hours; it is fine for them to sleep. Go to the emergency department or call 000 if any of these appear: drowsy or hard to wake; vomiting more than once; a headache that keeps getting worse; confusion, unusual behaviour or slurred speech; weakness or numbness in an arm or leg; unequal pupils or problems with vision; a seizure; clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears. For headache use paracetamol only; avoid aspirin and anti-inflammatory tablets unless a doctor says otherwise. No alcohol, sleeping tablets or driving for at least 24 hours.
source: healthdirect, Head injuries; NSW Health, Initial management of closed head injury in adults (discharge advice)

title: Blood-thinning medicine and head knocks
text: Blood-thinning medicines (for example warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, clopidogrel) make bleeding inside the head more likely after any knock. If the head may have struck the floor, arrange a medical assessment the same day even if the person seems well, and treat the warning signs in the head-knock section as an emergency.
source: NSW Clinical Excellence Commission, Post Fall Assessment and Management; healthdirect, Head injuries

title: If they fall again and cannot get up
text: Do not pull them up by the arms. Check for pain, bleeding or confusion first; if any is present, or they cannot move, keep them warm with a blanket and call 000. If they are uninjured, guide them slowly: roll onto the side, come up onto hands and knees, crawl to a sturdy chair, kneel facing it, bring one foot forward, push up to sit on the chair, and rest before standing. Consider a personal alarm pendant with fall detection so help can be called from the floor.
source: WA Health, Health advice following a fall; Stay On Your Feet (WA)

title: After coming home from hospital
text: Follow the discharge summary and take medicines exactly as listed; ask the pharmacist if anything is unclear. Book a GP review within a week and ask about a physiotherapy or falls-clinic referral and a medicines review. New confusion, sleepiness or a sudden change in behaviour after a hospital stay needs a same-day medical review. Check the skin over the tailbone, heels and hips daily if the person spends long periods sitting or lying.
source: WA Health, Health advice following a fall; NSW Health falls prevention resources

title: Reducing the chance of another fall
text: Remove loose rugs and cables from walkways; add night lights between bed and bathroom; wear firm, non-slip shoes rather than slippers; install grab rails by the toilet and shower; have vision and hearing checked; ask the GP or pharmacist to review medicines that cause dizziness or sleepiness; keep up strength and balance exercise; drink enough fluids through the day.
source: NSW Health / healthdirect falls prevention advice; Stay On Your Feet

title: Who to call
text: Call 000 if the person is unresponsive, cannot get up, has severe pain, a suspected fracture, or any head-injury warning sign. For advice at any hour call healthdirect on 1800 022 222 to speak with a registered nurse. See the GP for follow-up within a week of any fall.

title: If an ambulance was used (NSW)
text: Ambulance transport in NSW is not covered by Medicare and an invoice will arrive. Holders of a Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card, Commonwealth Seniors Health Card or DVA card are exempt; people with private health insurance have the fee paid by their fund. When the invoice arrives, claim the exemption online through Service NSW with the card number before the due date, or forward the invoice to the health fund.
source: NSW Government, Apply for a fee exemption or review; NSW Ambulance, Exemptions from fees
